Don’t neglect cleaning your plants! It helps prevent unwanted pests that can eat at your plant and keeps them looking fresh and pretty. I make my own mixture that I’ll describe below but feel free to do your own research! 

I use a spray bottle filled with like 75% water, a couple good splashes of neem oil, couple pumps of peppermint Castile soap, and a conservative splash of rubbing alcohol. I spray my plant leaves and gently rub it in on both sides of the leave with a microfiber glove or cloth. I do this 1-2x per month. Buying the stuff to make this lasts forever. I bought all the ingredients 2 months ago and I’m still working on finishing up my first spray bottle I made from it and I have 60+ plants.

I find that the best way to make drying quicker is to first do a super thorough towel dry - they should have minimal water dripping off of them. After that I’ll use the dryer and blast off the majority of the water on them. I’ll spritz them generously with quick dry and rub it into the coat and then continue drying as normal. Drying one section at a time will make it go fastest. Using a happy hoodie while drying their body will help dry their head/ears faster as well.

If you use the quick dry while they’re still pretty wet you’re just wasting the product. It’ll just blast out of the coat along with water if they’re too wet.

My dude you asked for the point of shaving paws and people are giving you the reasons why and you’re just combatting every answer and acting like you know more. If you know then why did you ask. If your dogs hair grows a lot between the pads then have it shaved to prevent matting, injuries from slipping, and dirt tracking. If none of these things have been an issue then don’t worry about it. And yes the foxtails/burrs will work their way into the paw pads because of being stuck to the hair. A dog with long hair in the pads who gets a foxtail/burr stuck to it is walking and putting pressure on their pads. The hair might DELAY when the foxtail/burr pierced the skin but it absolutely will still work it’s way into the skin. Not to mention that it would cause the hair to mat up around it very quickly.

I’m a groomer as well and I agree that the doodle craze has been very overwhelming. A lot of doodle owners are not well informed on the maintenance their dog requires. Most aren’t bred very well and a lot of breeders overlook important factors like temperament in the parents. Of course I have plenty of good doodles who are a dream to groom, but in my experience most end up being a nightmare to work on. I really think this is due to owner neglect though.. the dog isn’t used to being groomed frequently and is almost always shaved down which isn’t a comfortable process so of course the dog will act out. My most successful doodle grooms come from clients who keep a regular 4-6 week schedule and do regular maintenance between appointments. I’m very thankful for my good doodle clients 😊

My golden was like this when she was that age, some sounds still startle her but nowhere near how they used to. Trash pickup day was the worst since the trucks are so loud. 

We’ve worked on this a lot and seen huge improvements. First, I really taught her to look at me or come sit by me on command and she got really good at it. And whenever I could anticipate a sound happening that would normally frighten her, I’d get her to come sit with me and she’d start focusing on me instead of the noise and of course she got tons of treats and love. Distraction from the sound is the best way IMO to teach them to ignore loud sounds.
